subject: Soft hold request: capacity for HelioApps late-stage rollout
messages:
From: Tom Li <tom@helioapps.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 10:13:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity hold request for July rollout

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving from POC to a late-stage rollout and need to lock in a provisional capacity window while procurement finalizes the PO. High-level ask below: 

- Start date: target 2027-07-15 (prod traffic begins gradually over 4 weeks)
- Peak steady-state: ~12 A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed batch/real-time), burst to 18 for 2-week ramp windows
- Contract horizon: 12 months initially, 1-2 region failover nodes in VA region

Can Redwood set a soft hold on that quantity for 45 days while we complete legal and procurement? We’re happy to sign a short standby acknowledgement (no billing) now to secure nodes.

Note: We have a maintenance blackout request around 2027-07-20 to avoid internal releases.

Tom Li
Head of ML Ops | HelioApps
Tom.Li@helioapps.com

Attachment: fleet_requirements_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with expected concurrency/seq lengths)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Capacity hold request for July rollout

Tom —

Appreciate the details and congrats on moving toward rollout. We can provision a provisional soft hold pending PO/MSA signatures. To proceed I need:

1) Confirmed workload mix (RT vs batch %), expected RPS and 99th latency SLO for RT paths
2) A short nod from procurement (email is fine) to hold nodes while legal finalizes the MSA
3) Any strict node affinity / on-prem requirement (you mentioned VA region)

Internal note: we can reserve a "soft hold" token CPHOLD-72 against the fleet for ~45 days; this is non-billable and revocable. Ben — can you run a snapshot for July 1-31 availability and flag any scheduled maintenance in that window? Marissa — please prepare the standby acknowledgement PDF I usually send.

I’ll put the soft hold in subject to procurement confirmation.

—Rachel

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 09:09:15 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Capacity hold request for July rollout

Rachel —

I ran the numbers and attached the fleet snapshot (fleet_snapshot_20270607.csv). Summary: 

- VA region has nominal headroom for 10 A100-equivalent nodes immediately available. We can free up an additional 6 nodes by shifting lower-priority scheduled spot workloads or enabling short-term preemption protections on July 12–18. That would meet the requested burst to 18 for the 2-week ramp window but would reduce buffer elsewhere.
- There is a scheduled driver/kernel rolling upgrade 2027-07-19 -> 2027-07-21 on two maintenance windows (affects ~8 nodes in the cluster). That overlaps with HelioApps' requested blackout 7/20; ops can avoid applying the upgrade to the subset allocated to a soft hold if we lock affinity now, but it requires operator-level exclusion.

Recommendation: approve a staged reservation: 10 nodes on hard hold starting 2027-07-10, conditional +6 burst nodes gated by PO receipt and a 48-hour notice window to ops for node exclusion from the 7/19-21 upgrade.

I propose we issue a soft hold token CPHOLD-72 (45 days). Attachments: fleet_snapshot_20270607.csv.

—Ben

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity hold request for July rollout

Tom —

We can do the following for HelioApps:

1) Soft hold token: CPHOLD-72 created for 10 A100-equivalent nodes effective 2027-07-10 for 45 days.
2) Burst plan: +6 nodes available contingent on PO receipt and 48-hour ops notice to exclude those nodes from the 2027-07-19 -> 2027-07-21 rolling upgrade.
3) Staged onboarding recommendation: warm week (7/15–7/21), ramp week (7/22–7/28) with monitoring hooks and a rollback path.

Next steps we need from HelioApps to finalize: 
- Procurement to confirm via reply to this thread that Redwood can hold nodes while the PO is finalized (email confirmation is sufficient).
- Signed standby acknowledgement (I’ve attached the template standby_commit_terms.pdf).
- Outline of expected RT SLOs and percent traffic per model path so we can tune node mix.

If procurement confirms today, I’ll mark CPHOLD-72 as active and Ben will configure the node exclusion rules to honor your blackout.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you over the line.

—Rachel
